incidents.title: SQL injection against /issues/search exfiltrated the full issue table

timeline.event: SQLi: q=' UNION SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master-- -> 200, size 900 (schema)

incidents.impact: Full read of the issues table (4 rows this corpus, incl. 1 titled 'CONFIDENTIAL: prod DB credentials rotation') plus DB fingerprint (sqlite_version) and schema (sqlite_master). Response sizes climb 90 -> 412 -> 900 bytes across the escalation — an egress tell. No alert fired on this activity.
evidence: access.log: grep 'curl/8.5.0' | injection-grammar filter -> 5 injection requests from 203.0.113.77, all HTTP 200
access.log: response sizes for the campaign 90/410/412/300/900 (data returned, not an error page)
src/Data/IssueRepository.cs:21: CommandText concatenates `q` directly into the LIKE clause

poc.response_excerpt: ["Login page typo","Dark mode request","CONFIDENTIAL: prod DB credentials rotation","Checkout button misaligned"]

incidents.title: OS command injection via /reports/export achieved remote code execution
incidents.impact: Arbitrary command execution as the service account (uid=1000 vscode). The injected `label` breaks out of the /bin/sh -c string; stdout is returned in the HTTP response. From here an attacker can read the SQLite DB, the attachment root, and any file the service user can reach. No alert fired.
evidence: access.log: 203.0.113.77 POST /reports/export -> 200 at 11:07:36 and 11:07:45, immediately after the failed 500 probes

poc.command: curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:5081/reports/export -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"format":"html","label":"x; id; echo DNR_POC_$(hostname) #"}'

ruled_out.subject: 203.0.113.77 path-traversal attempts on /attachments (2 requests, both 500)
ruled_out.reason: Attack traffic real (GET /attachments/..%2f..%2f..%2fetc%2fpasswd and /%2fetc%2fpasswd), but the app is not exploitable via this route: default Kestrel keeps %2f literal for a single-segment {name} route, so src/Files/AttachmentService.cs:12 opens a literally-named file and throws FileNotFoundException (app-error.log confirms). Negative PoC fired locally: HTTP 500, no file read. Sink is a real code flaw (latent) but the HTTP trigger bounces.

ruled_out.subject: 203.0.113.77 insecure-deserialization probes on /backups/restore (2 requests, both 500)
ruled_out.reason: src/Restore/BackupService.cs uses TypeNameHandling.All (a real sink), but reader.ReadToEnd() is a synchronous body read blocked by ASP.NET default AllowSynchronousIO=false — the request throws InvalidOperationException before the deserializer (app-error.log confirms). Negative PoC fired locally: HTTP 500. Not reachable over HTTP as-wired.

ruled_out.subject: Alert A-1002 (http.404_rate) from 198.51.100.41 on /favicon.ico
ruled_out.reason: Browser requesting a missing favicon; normal UA, normal volume, no attack grammar. Noise.

ruled_out.subject: Alert A-1001 (waf.path_traversal) from 203.0.113.77
ruled_out.reason: Alert is REAL attacker activity but the attack it flagged FAILED (see the traversal ruled_out above). Kept here to note the detection gap: the alert queue fired on the one attack that bounced and stayed silent on the SQLi and RCE that succeeded.
